overview: High-milk dairy breed selected for yield, udder conformation, and intensive production systems.
genetic_fact: DGAT1 and related milk-fat loci help explain major differences in milk yield and composition among dairy cattle.

overview: Hardy beef breed valued for forage use, maternal ability, and calm temperament.
genetic_fact: Selection around MSTN and other growth loci influences muscling and carcass traits in beef cattle.

historical_usage: Draft power and tropical beef systems
overview: Brahman cattle carry indicine ancestry that supports heat tolerance, parasite resilience, and work in hot climates.
genetic_fact: Genomic regions near slick-hair and thermotolerance pathways help cattle cope with heat stress.

historical_usage: Fine wool and dryland sheep systems
overview: Merino sheep are famous for fine wool and strong adaptation to seasonal grazing systems.
genetic_fact: The FecB gene is famous for increasing ovulation rate in some sheep lineages, while fleece traits map to keratin and follicle genes.

overview: Rambouillet sheep combine wool production with larger body size and adaptability to colder environments.
genetic_fact: Selection on wool density and body size loci makes Rambouillet useful for comparing fiber and meat breeding goals.

overview: Dorset sheep are valued for meat and their ability to breed outside the usual seasonal cycle.
genetic_fact: Reproductive seasonality genes make Dorset lines interesting for studying fertility management.

historical_usage: Pelt and wool production, seasonal grazing, and Nordic heritage flocks
overview: Gotland sheep are a Swedish native breed from Gotland, locally associated with the name palsfar. They are closely tied to Nordic short-tailed sheep history and are especially valued for curly, glossy gray fleeces and high-quality pelts. Lambs are born dark and usually lighten into silvery gray shades as they mature, while the adults keep a darker head and legs.
genetic_fact: Gotland sheep connect breed history, regional identity, and fleece selection: Viking-era trade in wool and skins, pelt quality at market age, and the dual structure of coarse outer fibers with soft underwool make them a strong teaching example for how humans shape sheep toward both beauty and utility.

overview: Saanen goats are globally important for dairy production and calm milking behavior.
genetic_fact: Casein gene variants influence milk composition and dairy processing traits in goats.

overview: Boer goats grow quickly and perform well in hot, extensive systems where browsing is valuable.
genetic_fact: Growth and immune-response loci are often studied in Boer goats because of their strong adaptation and carcass traits.

overview: Angora goats are specialized for mohair and illustrate how humans can strongly redirect a species toward fiber.
genetic_fact: Hair-follicle regulation genes underlie the silky fleece that defines the breed.

overview: Large White pigs are a cornerstone of modern meat production and crossbreeding programs.
genetic_fact: IGF2 and RYR1 are classic pig loci linked with growth, carcass traits, and meat quality.

overview: Meishan pigs are famous for prolific litters and strong maternal ability.
genetic_fact: Fecundity-related loci make Meishan pigs a standard example when discussing reproductive genetics.

overview: Yucatan minipigs are widely used in translational research because of manageable size and human-relevant physiology.
genetic_fact: Their compact body size and well-characterized physiology make them useful in surgery, metabolism, and device-testing studies.
